post.description:
Copies a file from a local filesystem path into the CMS uploads directory and creates a content record.  The file is classified by its extension (video, image, or audio) and a thumbnail is generated automatically.

This endpoint is designed for **MCP tools** and other integrations that cannot perform multipart file uploads.  The API server must have read access to the given path.

**Example:**
```json
{"path": "/Users/me/Desktop/promo.jpg", "name": "Summer Promo"}
```

Converts a `.pptx` file into editable CMS templates — one template per slide.  Text, images, and shapes are preserved as individual elements that can be edited in the template builder or updated via the Fields API.

The API server must have read access to the given file path.

**Example:**
```json
{"path": "/Users/me/Desktop/promo.pptx", "name_prefix": "Summer Campaign"}
```

Each slide produces a template named `<prefix> — Slide N` with a linked Content record that can be added to playlists immediately.

schema.title: Response List Elements Api V1 Templates  Template Id  Elements Get

post.description:
Adds a new element to the template.  You specify the type, position, size, and optional label.  An ID is auto-assigned.  The HTML cache is rebuilt automatically.

**Example — add a labelled text element:**
```json
{
  "type": "text",
  "label": "headline",
  "x": 100, "y": 50,
  "width": 600, "height": 80,
  "props": {
    "content": "Breaking News",
    "fontSize": 48,
    "fontWeight": "bold",
    "color": "#ff0000"
  }
}
```

get.description: Returns one element by its UUID, including all its visual properties.

put.description: Partially update an element's position, size, label, or visual props.  Only fields you include are changed.  Props are **merged** — you can send just `{"props": {"color": "#ff0000"}}` to change only the colour without touching fontSize, content, etc.

delete.description: Permanently removes a single element from the template.  HTML cache is rebuilt.

get.description: Returns a standalone HTML page with all elements rendered as absolutely-positioned divs.  This is the URL that the web player loads in an iframe.  Embed this URL anywhere that accepts HTML.

Returns every element that has a **label** assigned, along with its full visual properties.  This is your map of what fields are available for external updates.

Any element type can carry a label — text, panel, image, or video.  The response includes position, size, and all type-specific props (colours, fonts, content, media IDs, etc.).

schema.title: Response List Fields Api V1 Templates  Template Id  Fields Get

put.description:
Quick endpoint to update a labelled text element's **content string**.  Send `{"value": "new text"}`.  The HTML is regenerated immediately.

For updating colours, fonts, position, or non-text elements, use the PATCH endpoint instead.

patch.description:
Update **any visual property** of a labelled element — text content, colour, font size, background colour, position, size, opacity, and more.  Only the fields you include are changed.

**Example — change a text field's colour and font size:**
```json
{"color": "#ff0000", "fontSize": 64}
```

**Example — reposition and recolour a panel:**
```json
{"x": 200, "y": 100, "backgroundColor": "#1a1a2e"}
```

**Example — update text content + styling in one call:**
```json
{"content": "SALE — 50% OFF", "color": "#ff0000", "fontSize": 72, "fontWeight": "bold"}
```

fields.title: Fields
fields.description:
Map of label → value. Each value can be:
• A **string** — shorthand to update only the text content.
• An **object** (FieldStyleUpdate shape) — update any combination of content, colour, fontSize, backgroundColor, position, size, etc.

BatchFieldUpdate.title: BatchFieldUpdate
BatchFieldUpdate.description:
Update multiple labelled fields in a single request.  Each key in
`fields` is the label name, and the value is either a plain string
(shorthand for updating text content only) or a FieldStyleUpdate object
for full control over styling.

Import a PowerPoint (.pptx) file into the CMS.  Each slide becomes
an editable Template with text, image, and panel elements preserved
from the original presentation.

The API server must have read access to the given path.

TemplateElement.title: TemplateElement
TemplateElement.description:
A single visual element on the template canvas.

Every element has a **type**, a position (x, y), a size (width, height),
and a **props** dict whose shape depends on the type.  Optionally assign
a **label** to make the element addressable via the Fields API.
